title: Distributed API rate limiter
learning_objectives: Propose and revise an inspectable architecture
problem_statement: Protect a login API with a per-key request budget while keeping admission decisions fast. Clarify accuracy, burst allowance and behavior during counter-store failure.

clarification_facts.acceptable_overrun: Must be explicitly negotiated; not silently assumed zero

progressive_constraints.title: One admission point
progressive_constraints.description: One gateway enforces a per-key budget; a path must exist from client to admission service.

progressive_constraints.title: Four gateways
progressive_constraints.description: At 5000 RPS with four gateways, explain which authority owns each key and whether the quota is exact or approximate.

progressive_constraints.title: Counter-store outage
progressive_constraints.description: A 50000 RPS credential-stuffing burst coincides with a twelve-second counter-store outage. Declare the fail-open/closed/lease policy.

progressive_constraints.title: Regional partition
progressive_constraints.description: Active regions cannot coordinate for ten seconds. State and bound the quota/availability tradeoff.

valid_architecture_families.name: Shared atomic counter
valid_architecture_families.description: Gateways use an atomic shared authority and an explicit outage policy.

valid_architecture_families.name: Sticky local counters
valid_architecture_families.description: Route a key consistently, quantify approximation and rebalance/failover behavior.

valid_architecture_families.name: Hierarchical leases
valid_architecture_families.description: A regional authority leases finite token blocks; edges must not spend expired leases.

common_misconceptions: A network call being fast in an example is not a measured p99 bound.
Fail-open during credential stuffing needs a bounded origin-protection policy.

hint_ladder.level_1: Trace four requests for one key through different gateways.
hint_ladder.level_2: Compare a shared atomic authority with key-sticky local ownership and state the coordination cost.
hint_ladder.level_3: Four independent 100/min counters allow 400 requests. An atomic authority preserves a global count; finite token leases trade communication for bounded outstanding quota. State what happens when the authority is unavailable.

consolidation: An admission design must name a quota authority, its consistency boundary and its outage policy. A structural declaration is evidence of the proposal, not measured latency or proof that an implementation is atomic.
fresh_transfer_question: How would your policy change for paid API usage where a small overrun is costly but requests may be retried?
coach_instructions: One clear question at a time. Inspect actual graph and stated assumptions. Do not grade prose by keywords or require a vendor name. Numeric assumptions are learner declarations, not measured performance. Explain when asked, require teach-back, and preserve alternative valid designs. Do not silently edit the diagram.
